summary: The work reads as quiet observational photography built around ordinary neighborhoods, small businesses, lived-in architecture, domestic fragments, plants, thresholds, and human trace. The strongest opportunity direction is photobook, artist book, zine, small press, independent bookstore, and quiet documentary/photo publication ecosystems rather than commercial galleries or market-style events.
dominant_subjects: laundry, fences, stairs, paths, yards, and thresholds
human traces without dominant human subjects
best_formats: small group exhibition with strong thematic fit
artist_statement_phrases: the quiet infrastructure of daily life
small places that carry lived time
architecture as a record of habit and care

portfolio_bodies_to_create.title: Neighborhood Memory
portfolio_bodies_to_create.description: A sequence of ordinary streets, homes, plants, shops, and small architectural details that suggest lived time and human presence without direct portraiture.

portfolio_bodies_to_create.title: Human Trace
portfolio_bodies_to_create.description: Images of spaces shaped by use: thresholds, laundry, fences, shopfronts, yards, signs, and plants.

portfolio_bodies_to_create.title: Small Press Sequence
portfolio_bodies_to_create.description: A tight photobook/zine-oriented edit emphasizing repetition, atmosphere, and slow accumulation.
